prompt: In many towns and cities, online retailers have taken a large share of the trade that once went to shops on the high street. Do the advantages of this shift outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
The convenience of buying online is not seriously in dispute, and neither is the fact that shops are closing. What the argument usually misses is that these are not the same subject. The first is about how people acquire goods; the second is about what a town centre is for.

On the buying itself, the advantages are decisive and widely distributed. Prices are lower for a structural reason rather than a temporary one — a seller with no shopfront has costs a seller with one cannot avoid — and range is transformed for anyone outside a large city, where the alternative was never a better shop but no shop at all. Delivery is also, quietly, an accessibility measure: it reaches people whose hours, health or dependants had made an afternoon in town a serious undertaking.

The losses are real, but they are mostly not losses of shopping. Retail work was one of the last large sources of flexible local employment requiring no qualification, and the warehouse and courier jobs replacing it are neither local nor, in most cases, on comparable terms. More fundamentally, the high street was doing a second job that nobody was paying for: it was the reason people with no particular business with each other were in the same place at the same time. Shops financed that, and online retail does not.

So the advantages outweigh the disadvantages as a matter of shopping, and the interesting question is what follows from that. If the high street's value was mainly commercial, its decline is an efficiency gain and empty units are a transitional problem. If its value was mainly civic, then something has been dismantled by accident, and it will have to be paid for deliberately if it is wanted — through libraries, health centres, markets and housing rather than through a subsidy to shops that are not coming back.
title: Online shopping and the high street
